instruction.text: Round the number to the nearest thousand and select the answer on the number line.

Mr Carson is carrying out a survey on the number of <t-yellow>animals</t-yellow> in his farm.  Fill in the gaps in the table by rounding the <t-blue>number</t-blue> to the <t-purple>nearest thousand</t-purple>.

instruction.text: Round the volume of liquid in the measuring jug to the nearest thousand and fill in the gap.

Geoffrey the blacksmith is forging a new sword in his workshop. He is trying to work out the average temperature the metal reaches. Round the temperature shown on the thermometer to the nearest thousand and fill in the gap.

Freya has a secret number in her head. It is made up of the following digits: 5, 2, 4, and 4. When rounded to the nearest thousand, the number is 3,000. Select the number that could be Freya’s secret number.

Frank sells lemonade from his lemonade stand every weekend. He calculates that last weekend he used 1,300 lemons on Friday, 2,124 on Saturday and 3,182 on Sunday. Work out the total amount of lemons Frank used last weekend to the nearest thousand.

atoms.a: First, round the amount of lemons he used on each day.
Next, add the rounded sums together.

atoms.b: The total amount of lemons used by Frank to the nearest thousand is <mat><gap>6000</gap></mat>.
